claims.text: The proposed Ti–Nb–Ta–V–Zr high-entropy alloy has a bcc structure.
The as-cast Ti–Nb–Ta–V–Zr alloy is chemically disordered.
Atomic-size and electronegativity mismatches in the as-cast alloy produce significant local lattice distortions.
The local lattice distortions in the disordered alloy are detrimental to coherent phonon formation.
Annealing near 800°C followed by quenching will enhance and retain short-range chemical order in Ti–Nb–Ta–V–Zr.
Annealing-induced short-range order aligns atoms into local regions with similar sizes and bonding characteristics.
Enhanced short-range chemical order reduces local lattice distortions.
Reducing local lattice distortions modifies the electronic density of states.
Short-range ordering softens specific phonon modes.
The ordered arrangement facilitates more coherent vibrational modes.
The proposed changes in lattice distortion and phonon behavior strengthen electron–phonon coupling.
Stronger electron–phonon coupling enhances Cooper-pair formation.
Annealed samples with greater short-range order will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples will show measurable phonon softening or other changes in electron–phonon coupling parameters relative to the as-cast alloy.
Atom probe tomography and high-resolution diffraction can quantify the induced short-range order and assess whether phase segregation occurred.
